ruled_out.claim: AIST++ can supply block A, the shared audio->movement skeleton. ELIMINATED for this corpus. What varies between AIST++ tracks is the dance GENRE, not the acoustics, and the movement follows the genre.
ruled_out.method: Direct replication of Burger et al. 2013's stimulus-level design on all 60 AIST++ tracks: one row per track, movement averaged over every dancer and frame, audio averaged over the track, bootstrap CIs over tracks; then the same correlations with genre and tempo partialled out; then the share of between-track movement variance explained by the genre label alone; then a check of whether audio can recover genre at all.
ruled_out.evidence: Not one published correlation replicates, and several invert. Pulse clarity -> quantity of motion: Burger +0.62, here -0.078 (CI [-0.341, +0.169]). Low-band flux -> head speed: +0.73 vs -0.102. High-band flux -> hand speed: +0.65 vs -0.321. High-band flux -> hand spread: +0.57 vs -0.396 (CI excludes zero, wrong sign). The audio features do vary across the corpus (CV 0.16 to 0.68), so this is not a range restriction. The explanation is the corpus design: the genre label alone explains 0.835 of between-track variance in quantity of motion, 0.916 in centre-of-mass speed, 0.879 in vertical bounce amplitude and 0.955 in footfall rate. With genre and tempo partialled out, every audio-movement correlation collapses to between -0.18 and +0.21 with CIs spanning zero. AIST++ is choreographed street dance whose music was chosen to match the style, so the arrow runs genre -> both music and movement; Burger's participants moved freely to varied music, where the arrow runs music -> movement. The shared component is real and highly reliable (split-half up to 0.94 for footfall rate) — it is simply not acoustic. Block A therefore needs free-dancing data; the Oslo club-dancing EDM mocap (Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0) is the corpus for it.

ruled_out.claim: AIST++ needs a per-track audio-motion sync offset: the dance is period-locked but phase-random against the music because each track's motion clock is shifted by an unknown constant. ELIMINATED.
ruled_out.method: Fit one offset per music id as the R-weighted circular mean of per-clip footfall beat phases, using only half of each track's clips; validate on the held-out half, then test the SAME offset on a channel it was not fitted to (vertical bounce minima). A genuine clock offset shifts every channel of a clip equally, so it must transfer.
ruled_out.evidence: The hypothesis looked strong: clips of one track agreed on a phase across different choreographies and dancers (concentration R = 0.59), the per-track estimate was split-half stable (r = 0.83), and on held-out clips the correction lifted footfall beat alignment from +0.019 (CI [-0.006, +0.044], i.e. chance) to +0.128 (CI [+0.103, +0.153]) — above the audio beat-trigger baseline's +0.101. It still fails the transfer test: on vertical bounce minima of held-out clips the raw signal is already aligned (+0.0382, CI [+0.0230, +0.0541]) and applying the footfall-fitted offset DESTROYS that alignment (+0.0081, CI [-0.0068, +0.0228]). There is no missing clock offset. What the corpus actually contains is a channel-specific phase: vertical bounce sits on the beat with no correction (the Toiviainen 2010 / Burger 2013 prediction), while footfall phase belongs to the choreography, which in street dance is routinely off the beat. Provenance: lightsem/data/sync.py, kept as a documented refutation with the fitting code intact.

ruled_out.claim: A causal temporal encoder over openl3 audio embeddings can predict the RPMC-L2 stage-lighting scene vector (6-dim HSV summary), i.e. a trained macro layer can replace the hand-written rule table by regressing audio -> absolute lighting state.
ruled_out.method: Marginal-contribution test on per-song-centred targets, held-out songs. (1) Ridge fits for audio-only, persistence-only (y's own lags 0.1-4.0 s), and AR+audio; the audio claim stands or falls on AR+audio minus AR, not on audio's absolute score. (2) A 2.36M-param causal transformer trained 40 epochs as the strong-model control. (3) A lag-shift control: audio-light correlation recomputed with y shifted +-30 s WITHIN each song, since real frame-level coupling must peak at lag 0 while slow co-drift does not. Split is by song (hash), so no venue appears in both train and test.
ruled_out.evidence:
Refuted by a marginal-contribution test, not by a weak model.

SETUP: 140 songs, 126,332 frames @10 Hz, split BY SONG (99/23/18). Target is
the per-song-CENTRED scene vector (35-65% of raw variance is between-song
venue palette, which is given, not predicted). Metric R2_within on held-out songs.

TRAINED MODEL (2,359,769 params, causal, 40 epochs, RTX 5070):
  test R2_within (now)   = -0.0071
  best epoch             = 0 (before learning anything)
  train loss 0.1554 -> 0.0418 while val R2 fell -0.004 -> -0.445 (memorisation)

BASELINES (all below the zero point):
  per-song mean oracle   = -0.0000  <- zero point
  best fair linear       = -0.1091

CEILING PROBE (the decisive measurement):
  audio only             = -0.1091
  persistence only (AR)  = +0.7083
  AR + audio             = +0.7035
  audio's marginal gain  = -0.0049   <- NEGATIVE

Lighting is ~71% predictable from its own past 0.1-4.0 s, with NO audio.
Adding 512 audio dims on top of that does not help.

TIME-SHIFT CONTROL: correlation of audio vs light, y shifted within-song:
  lag -30s 0.27325 | lag 0s 0.14104 | lag +30s 0.17044
Peak at lag -30s, MINIMUM near zero. Real frame-level coupling
must peak at lag 0. This is slow co-drift over minutes, not coupling.

RETRACTION: the earlier data-audit finding of "20-36x audio-light correlation
vs shuffled control" is withdrawn as evidence. The shuffle destroyed
within-song structure, so it tested the wrong null. The lag-shift control is
the correct one and it fails.

ruled_out.claim: AIST Dance DB audio is a usable corpus for validating EDM structure detection and anticipatory (build-up -> drop) lighting control. ELIMINATED. AIST tracks are short, loudness-normalised dance loops whose energy dynamic range is ~5x too small to contain the build-up/drop structure the anticipation layer exists to detect. Also eliminated as the SOLE explanation of the weak first result: 'the segmentation/anticipation detector is broken' -- a synthetic control proves the detector localises real drops to <1 s.
ruled_out.method:
Two-hypothesis discrimination with a SYNTHETIC CONTROL SIGNAL. The first anticipation run on 5 AIST tracks gave recall 0.000 on 3/5, and on the one track scoring 0.800 the rate-matched random baseline was 0.625 (i.e. no skill). Two competing explanations were separated rather than assumed: H1 detector broken; H2 corpus has no structure.

probe_control_synthetic.py synthesises EDM-shaped audio (kick on the beat, rising riser + amplitude ramp through an 8 s build, wide bright drop section, quiet breakdown) with drops at KNOWN times 16.0 s and 36.0 s, and runs the IDENTICAL librosa laplacian-segmentation + labelling + anticipation pipeline over it. Energy dynamic range (RMS p90/p10, std/mean) is measured on the synthetic track and on 10 real AIST tracks for direct comparison.

probe_anticipation_baselines.py then prices the anticipation claim against THREE nulls rather than a bare number: (1) rate-matched uniform-random cues, 500 draws; (2) a metronome cue process at the same rate, 20 phases; (3) a NULL TRACK of steady-state audio with no drops, to expose a trigger-happy detector. Scoring uses precision and nearest-cue lead time, because recall saturates for every method once the credit window is wide.
ruled_out.evidence:
=== ENERGY DYNAMIC RANGE (the decisive contrast) ===
  synthetic EDM control : RMS p90/p10 = 18.27   std/mean = 0.726
  AIST median of 10     : RMS p90/p10 =  3.76   std/mean ~ 0.45
  per-track AIST p90/p10: mBR0 6.45, mBR1 4.16, mBR2 3.45, mBR3 4.06,
                          mBR4 4.79, mBR5 5.42, mHO0 2.95, mHO1 2.68,
                          mHO2 2.86, mHO3 3.24
AIST segment energies sit inside a 0.475-0.518 band on a 0-1 normalised scale -- essentially no build-up/drop contour exists.

=== H1 REFUTED: the detector works on audio that HAS structure ===
After fixing a labelling defect (below), drop localisation error against the known synthetic drops is 0.44 s and 0.57 s.
Anticipation on the synthetic track, scored honestly:
  REAL      precision 1.000   nearest-lead 2.78 s +- 0.08 s
  RANDOM    precision 0.495 +- 0.208   nearest-lead 4.36 s +- 2.48 s
  METRONOME precision 0.500 +- 0.106   nearest-lead 3.37 s +- 1.66 s
  precision z vs random = +2.42
The lead-time STD is the sharpest discriminator: 0.08 s real vs 2.48 s random. It is not merely hitting the window, it is hitting a consistent phase of the build.

=== NULL TRACK CONTROL (not trigger-happy) ===
On steady-state drop-free audio the cue rate collapses 0.146 Hz -> 0.021 Hz. RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, NOT HIDDEN: the labeller still tags 3 spurious 'drop' segments on that audio, so boundary detection is solid while the functional labeller is the weak link.

=== WHY RECALL WAS THE WRONG HEADLINE ===
At 7 cues / 48 s with a 12 s credit window, rate-matched random cues reach 0.816 recall vs the real detector's 0.875 -- a margin near zero. Recall saturates and cannot separate methods; precision and lead-time concentration can, and do (z = +2.42).

=== THREE REAL BUGS THE CONTROL EXPOSED (none visible from AIST) ===
1. librosa.util.sync emits one MORE column than beat frames, so a cluster-change index could equal len(beat_times) -> IndexError crash.
2. QUANTILE labelling mislabels loud segments: a 0.613-energy segment was labelled 'breakdown' while the track max was 0.620, because it sat below the 0.66 quantile. Localisation error was 3.23 s / 6.66 s. Fixed by labelling RELATIVE TO THE TRACK'S OWN ENERGY RANGE plus an explicit drop-follows-build-up rule -> 0.44 s / 0.57 s.
3. THE METRIC PUNISHED BETTER ANTICIPATION (see the companion rule-out).

=== CONSEQUENCE ===
AIST stays correct for pose/choreography work and is fine as a RENDERING input, but structure-detection and anticipation claims must be validated on EDM-98 / EDM-CUE (arXiv 2603.08759, HF disco-eth/edm-cue), NOT yet downloaded. Any anticipation number quoted on AIST audio is uninformative about the mechanism.

ruled_out.claim: Using sound as a PIVOT modality rescues the mapping: learn motion -> sound on AIST (which has motion+audio) and sound -> light on RPMC-L2 (which has audio+light), then compose them to get motion -> light. This is proposed as a way around the absence of any dataset pairing motion with stage lighting.
ruled_out.method: Attack the chain at its SECOND link, which is shared with the already-refuted direct mapping, so link 1 never has to be built. By the data processing inequality, motion -> sound -> light makes motion conditionally independent of light given sound; the chain's ceiling is therefore what the MOTION-RECOVERABLE PART of sound explains about light. Prior AIST measurement (probe1_pose_vs_audio.py, 263 sequences) shows motion and audio share only a slow envelope: R2 = 0.0019 at 0.1 s but r = 0.65 at 8 s smoothing. So link 1 was given an ORACLE: assume motion recovers the audio envelope PERFECTLY at timescale w and nothing faster, then band-split audio (centred uniform filter) and measure each band's marginal R2_within over a persistence (AR) baseline on held-out songs. Deliberately generous: the smoothing is CENTRED so it uses the future, and the oracle is perfect within band; a real causal motion->sound model gets strictly less than this bound.
ruled_out.evidence:
The bound is at or below zero at EVERY timescale, so the chain cannot work.

Persistence baseline (lighting's own past 0.1-4.0 s, no audio): R2_within +0.7083

Marginal contribution of each audio band OVER persistence, held-out songs:
  full audio (no split)   -0.0049
  slow band  w=1s         -0.0060
  slow band  w=2s         -0.0082
  slow band  w=4s         -0.0099
  slow band  w=8s         -0.0182   <- the motion-recoverable band, ORACLE link 1
  slow band  w=16s        -0.0313
  fast band  w=1s         -0.0027   <- best of ANY band
Best marginal over all timescales: -0.0027. Every value is NEGATIVE.

Note the ordering: the slow bands are the WORST. The band motion can actually
reach (34% of audio variance at 8 s) hurts more than the full signal
(-0.0182 vs -0.0049), and it degrades monotonically as the window widens
(1s -0.0060 -> 16s -0.0313). The pivot bottleneck selects for
exactly the component of audio that is least useful about light.

This is an ORACLE bound on link 1, so it is not a statement about how good a
motion->sound model could be made. Even a perfect one inherits -0.0182.

Root cause is a composition-of-ceilings problem, not two independent bugs:
  link 1 (motion->sound) passes only a slow envelope  [AIST: 0.0019 @0.1s, r=0.65 @8s]
  link 2 (sound->light) has zero marginal signal at all timescales  [this probe]
Cross-modal transfer moves only REDUNDANT information (multimodal-ai lecture 08),
so a pivot chain can only pass information present in BOTH intersections. Here
that intersection is empty.

do_not_retry.item: Do not accept visible movement as learned music control; map-only and untrained controls must remain visible in the report.
Do not treat low BPM-phase R2 as proof of musicality: noise-dominated motion also has low phase R2.
Do not repeat this unchanged one-seed recipe as a confirmed solution: keep failed audio-conditioning gates until an explicit mechanism change.
Do not ban beat inputs from these failures; beat presence was not isolated as their cause.
Do not use latent distribution/alignment gates alone to call dancing-light output successful.
Do not remove beat features as a universal cure; latest user explicitly permits them.
Do not widen legacy pan to+-180 without world-coordinate ray/visibility checks.

results.statement: A causal Conformer with three heads — deterministic block A, event hazard block B, conditional-flow block C — trained on AIST++ produces light that lands on the music like dance-derived light does, with a feature distribution close to it and sampled variety a regression head cannot give.
results.why_it_failed: refuted [recipe_conditional]: Two fixes follow from the mechanism, and neither is 'train longer'. First, the block A / block C boundary was drawn from the literature and should be redrawn from the Stage 0b audit: on this corpus almost nothing clears the identity baseline, so almost everything belongs in the SAMPLED block, not the regressed one. Regressing an unpredictable channel does not produce a cautious estimate, it produces a flat line, and a flat line makes bad light. Second, the flow head samples each frame independently given the trunk state, so its variety is high-frequency jitter rather than the burst-and-rest structure real dance has; it needs to condition on its own previous output. Both are v2 work. Meanwhile the diagnostic to keep is the one that caught this: report the event RATE and the circular-shift null next to every Light-BAS, because a model can raise alignment and lose the comparison by flashing more.

results.statement: A factorised audio-light critic trained with time-shift, other-song AND beat-trigger negatives on bar-synchronous tokens learns something beyond beat and loudness: it separates real authored light from beat-trigger light on held-out songs above chance, its best-of-8 ranking over rectified-flow samples changes when the critic is projected to its nearest additive model, and best-of-8 beats random-of-8 on human 'fits the music'. Without the beat-trigger negative it collapses to a beat detector and rewards the mode the model already occupies.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted critic-pair-accuracy up, observed up (Δ +0.393)

results.statement: A learned group-effects decoder (Anton's mixture of light: a shared type-masked head on the frozen trunk and operator head emitting per-group intensity envelope, palette, effect id, rate in beats, phase spread and density, expanded to DMX by a deterministic effects engine) trained on authored light through a differentiable histogram renderer with random-rig dropout beats the hand-written conductor on Value- and onset-matched held-out songs: FID vs conductor beats a shuffled-donor control by > 2x, BAS is not lower without more onsets, raters prefer it on 'fits the music' with a CI excluding 50% at n >= 20, and it transfers to an unseen patch better than channel-copy.
results.why_it_failed: refuted: predicted fid-light-kinetic down, observed up (Δ +886.079)

results.statement: A look sampler that HOLDS its sampled look between cues fired by the calibrated look-change hazard (refractory 2 s, rate matched to the corpus) reproduces the authored corpora's look-transition statistics better than a per-frame sampler and than a shuffled donor, and lands on the beat no worse than the hand-written conductor at no higher onset density.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted cue-transition-distance down, observed down (Δ -2.012)

results.statement: Authored hobby/game light shows are lighting corpora, not tempo corpora: on xLights free .xsq sequences (where the song is on disk) and Beat Saber lightshow maps, audio predicts the group-level event stream and envelopes on held-out shows with AP_audio - AP_time-shift >= +0.15 and AP_audio >= AP_beat-trigger + 0.05, causal and offline. A corpus that fails stays out of every loss.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted event-ap-lift-audio-marginal up, observed up (Δ +0.3553)

results.statement: Conditioning on whole-track structure -- section label and time to the next drop -- is worth more than anything else the offline setting buys, because structure is where the largest measured effect in this project's data lives.
results.why_it_failed: refuted: predicted light-bas-minus-shift-null up, observed down (Δ -0.0282)

results.statement: Dance is not a category error for light. Light derived from real dance motion through the hybrid conductor (dance envelopes, audio-phased transients), brightness-matched against a 30-line audio beat trigger on the same music, is preferred by a blind rater on at least one of two questions: 'which is on the music?' and 'which looks like a lighting engineer did it?'. If the beat trigger wins both, block C (the sampled style residual) leaves the product.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted human-preference-winrate up, observed up (Δ +0.35)

results.statement: Feeding the group decoder the hazard features of its OWN emitted cues (teacher-forced in training, autoregressive in 1 s blocks at inference) raises its held-out cue-timing lift above the audio-only decoder on Just Dance visual and RPMC-L2, recovering part of the margin the with-hazard operator head holds (3.17x vs 2.35x on JD); decoder size alone does not.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted event-ap-lift-audio-marginal up, observed up (Δ +0.0017)

results.statement: A beat-conditioned A/B/C sequence model with correct world aiming and independent emitted-light checks will produce more physically valid visible movement than the current no-clock body-v2 prototype while retaining measurable nonbeat audio control.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive [recipe_conditional]: World-target geometry repairs emitted-light visibility (1.0 vs 0.0); old weights with the same map also reach 1.0. The new recipe does not establish musical motion control: only 0.025 of40songs pass same-beat spectral-response/noise criteria, and A alignment advantage is -0.2130; report event selectivity's separate pass without hiding these failures. A future motion-control change must be evaluated on emitted trajectories with fixed rhythm and paired noise, retaining local timing checks.

results.statement: Higher declared simulated actuator limits restore more fast motion under the same full-track convex target-fitting objective.
results.why_it_failed: inconclusive: predicted motion-light-angular-band-amplitude up, observed up (Δ +0.568562)

problem.title: Sound -> light for concerts/festivals, TRAINED ON DANCE datasets (LightSem v2): generative audio -> light on dance-derived targets
problem.description: Accepted representation-first implementation 2026-09-10. Build convincing music-driven stage lighting. Music is the only playback input; an internal generated skeleton/motion sequence is explicitly allowed. Hybrid measured audio dynamics may control brightness and movement intensity. Quiet passages must remain visible but restrained. Establish clean motion-source and temporal-codec quality before audio training. Prior human review rejects flashing/juggling reconstructions and excessive Shpongle movement; only the incumbent audio-to-descriptions-to-pose path is currently visually convincing. Glare improvement is useful but does not establish visible head-brightness dynamics. Exploration seed0; confirm only qualifying finalist and matched baseline at seed1. Accelerated BF16/compile/prefetch in matched arms, no earlier 2–3h ceiling. Historical nulls and gates remain valid.

updates.text: 2026-09-03 rev. 2 (Anton's correction): dance datasets are the TRAINING SET for a sound->light model; no music-to-dance generation at inference. Rev. 1's 'latent dancer' inference path is withdrawn; generators survive only as an optional offline pseudo-labelling teacher (PLAN.md section 8). Runbooks rb-ls2-00..05 rewritten accordingly.

2026-09-04 rev. 3: integrated four Perplexity reasoning passes (audio->light design; music-induced-movement science; causal model + latency; dataset audit degenerated, replaced by direct source checks) and Anton's note on extracting motion from video with pose models. Targets split into deterministic skeleton / event point-process / sampled style residual; rig mapping follows the body; two-path deployment (transients on a 10-20 ms DSP path) because ITU-R BT.1359-1 detectability is +45 ms when sound leads. New runbooks 00b (predictability audit) and 00c (late-lights + category-error tests) run BEFORE any training.

2026-09-04 Stage 0b resolved in two halves (exp-002, exp-003). AIST++ cannot supply block A: genre explains 0.65-0.96 of between-track movement variance and Burger 2013 does not replicate, several correlations invert. Free dancing to EDM can: held-out-track R2 +0.30 for the shared movement curve on Oslo, drop/breakdown ratio 1.7-2.5x with Cohen's d up to 2.55. The binding constraint moves from 'is there a signal' to 'how much free-dance data can we get'.

2026-09-04 implementation pass complete (exp-004..exp-008): descriptor extractor (mocap and video), constant-tempo beat grid, canonical-rig conductors, evaluation suite with nulls, 9.3 M causal Conformer with three heads, streaming inference, blind A/B harness; 14 of 14 verification checks. Stage 1 light gates fail (+0.017 vs real-mapped +0.216); operator head passes (+0.31 lift, z 3.66); latency budget met.

2026-09-04 repair pass (exp-009): the Stage 1 audio bus read up to 375 ms of the future through librosa defaults; fixed, retrained, held-out block A R2 +0.0438 -> +0.0192, which is the size of the artefact. Event-rate calibration did not raise Light-BAS (predicted mechanism wrong). The surplus light events come from the sampled channels' 11-452x corpus HF energy. Product pivoted to the offline pre-rendered path (rb-ls2-07, PLAN rev. 6).

2026-09-04 Stage 0c category test (exp-010): dance-derived hybrid light beats the beat trigger 8-1 (1 equal) on 'looks like a lighting engineer', ties 5-4 on 'on the music'; one rater, 10 brightness-matched AIST++ pairs. Category error rejected directionally; block C stays. Rater's tell for 'not an engineer' was change rate, the same defect the model carries.

2026-09-04 Stage 8 queued (rb-ls2-08): 338 Just Dance gameplay captures (22.0 h, full songs, one filmed stylised coach or several -- each coach its own channel; research-only). Three signals: coach motion for block A/C, hand-animated background lighting as a designed show for HEAD B, full-song structure for H-C. Decision measurement is the held-out-song predictability audit. Extraction launched 15:00 with YOLO26m-pose at 960 after a six-clip trial (solos and multi-coach at >= 0.998 coverage per coach).

2026-09-04 Stage 7 (rb-ls2-07), three of four hypotheses tested. H-A (exp-012): the look-ahead ceiling fails both gates -- with the whole track visible, held-out block A R2 on AIST++ is -0.009 against the causal +0.019 and the light gates do not move; the corpus binds, not the model. H-B (exp-011): spectral matching is the largest lever found -- a causal one-pole per channel fitted to the corpus above-6 Hz energy takes model Light-BAS from +0.018 to +0.293 (real-mapped +0.211), FID 67 -> 20, light events 86 -> 35 per clip against 30 real, diversity not falling; the 12 Hz filter the hypothesis named does nothing, the mismatch sits near 0.2 Hz; zero-phase at matched cutoffs scores the same, so the offline path removes lag, not jitter. H-D (exp-013): audio alone does not anticipate an operator's scene change 4 s ahead (offline margin -0.02, CI spanning zero); a 10x first result was a leak through target-derived hazard features under a symmetric window, caught by the shift control. H-C waits for the Just Dance corpus.

2026-09-04 (evening) Stage 9 queued (rb-ls2-09-designed-light, PLAN.md rev. 8 section 6.9). Anton's reading of the shipped Just Dance model: decent, not human. Five outside passes with the full brief (Perplexity deep research x1, reasoning x4: audio decomposition, datasets in two halves, multimodal methods, mixture of light) plus Skip-BART (arXiv:2506.01482) and SeqLight (arXiv:2605.03660) read in full agree on the diagnosis: the bottleneck is the target (dance is a weak proxy; coaches agree at r 0.22-0.42), the hand-written conductor, and the absence of human preference -- not the trunk, causality or the amount of dance. Deep-research verdict: 'another music-to-motion transformer will not close the gap; the project needs authored lighting intent, a learned hierarchical planner, and a preference model that tells deliberate composition from synchronised motion'. Datasets: no public, commercially clean corpus of professional DMX programming exists; RPMC-L2 (all 699 now cached, CC-BY-4.0, no waveform) is the only public stage-domain set; authored light exists at scale in xLights free .xsq sequences (~556, ~25-40 h, audio not included) and Beat Saber lightshow maps (v3 group event boxes with phase-spread filters, verified on the API); console show files only by contract. Seven hypotheses queued: H-G stems (audit-gated), H-H corpus predictability gate, H-I group-effects decoder (the mixture of light, SeqLight's split), H-J section planner on the knobs, H-K factorised critic with beat-trigger negatives as best-of-N, H-L Bradley-Terry knobs from 200-400 pairs, H-M frozen encoder vs random projection. Rule-outs added: AR light LM decoder, RL on the flow head before the critic gate, type-MoE in the trunk, section/chord/LRA/timbre bus channels, Jukebox/CLAP, fixture-token decoder before console data, product training on research corpora.

2026-09-05: Stage 9 (rb-ls2-09) run end to end; H-H, H-G, H-M, H-J, H-K directional-only, H-I refuted as built, H-L open (exp-017..023). Reading: the authored corpora on disk (RPMC-L2, Just Dance visual, Beat Saber) support learning WHEN a look changes and the corpus's look statistics, not per-frame or per-bar light levels; the decent-not-human gap is not closed by stems, a frozen encoder, a regressed or sampled group decoder, a bar planner or a critic reranker. Engine diagnostic: with the phase spread zeroed the v1 decoder's Light-BAS minus null is +0.51 (conductor +0.13) at fewer events than the conductor, so the BAS miss was the engine; FID_light and the missing human test carry the verdict. Next: cue-based rendering from the calibrated look-change hazard, scored on cue timing and look-transition statistics; the H-L human preference study; console show files for level design.

2026-09-08: H-L now has an analysed 39-pair pilot from Anton, not an empty ratings file. Repaired rating resume/validation and song-grouped preference fitting; held-out preference prediction accuracy 56.4% music fit, 59.0% designed appearance, both conditional intervals include 50%. No H-L gate passes; fresh fitted-vs-default and BAS gates remain unmeasured. Candidate settings saved, no defaults changed. Current pair videos have median 16.1% screen-luma mismatch despite close DMX metric matching; verified blinder metric/renderer discrepancy, and five same-title training counterparts need audio identity verification. Next comparisons need corrected matching and explicit wave/colour controls, which the original conductor-knob pairs do not test. problem.synthesis:
STATE OF KNOWLEDGE — 2026-09-08, continuation audit + incremental primary-source literature review.

Scope: pre-rendered audio -> stage lighting; whole-song context allowed; dance is training supervision only. The old causal-only/no-experiments synthesis is superseded. Current learned renderer uses the descriptor/event/style model with ConductorHybrid. Stage9 GroupEngine and generic CLI are separate entry points.

Local evidence: repeated tuning of stems, frozen audio features, model size, per-bar level regression, six-moment group decoding and critic/cue recipes did not close the designed-appearance gap. Strong synchronization scores can coexist with poor aesthetics. Historical supports/directional-only records are not blanket product gates. GroupDecoder is not a faithful Skip-BART/SeqLight implementation: it omits autoregressive light tokens, histogram targets and learned temporal decomposition. Existing recurrence analysis retains boundaries but not motif memory. Per-bar regression therefore does not rule out explicit motif reuse.

Human pilot:39ratings, one rater,29registered song groups. Held-out preference-model accuracy56.4%/59.0% with intervals including chance; music accuracy equals its majority-side baseline and appearance logloss0.739 is worse than0.693 chance. Fresh generated-candidate-vs-default wins are unmeasured. These ratings do not test new GroupEngine wave/colour controls. Median screen-luma mismatch16.1%; the blinder metric squares dimmer while the renderer is linear. Preserve old data/scores, version the correction, verify canonical audio identity and material matching before fresh preference claims.

New literature adds implementable SLS/EUBO preference acquisition, editable light-object layers (Glow with the Flow), explicit hierarchical/repetition representations, Beat This timing models and Raveform annotation access. Transfer to LightSem is untested. Glow with the Flow itself reports that synchronization/congruence ratings miss repetition and colour-richness defects. SeqLight weight release is not verified. RPMC is video-derived colour supervision, not professional DMX logs; no newly usable authored-control corpus was established.

Next experiments, in order of dependencies: material/metric validation; isolated beat benchmark; explicit recurrence-memory vs equally varied no-memory composition; active vs random pair acquisition; histogram/assignment oracle followed only conditionally by matched audio-conditioned training; independently reviewed authored-look oracle to measure renderer/planner capability. Budgets and thresholds in the report are proposals, not preregistrations. Confirm primary outcomes, independence unit and gates before execution; do not interpret an oracle failure as a uniquely identified cause.

No new training/rendering/GPU job or experiment closure was performed in this review. Additional Just Dance extraction remains a separate process; freeze and audit completed features before using new data. Existing interpretation debt and statuses are not cleared by this synthesis.
